\chapter{Se Habla Espanol --- Nobody in Particular}
\label{ch:se-impersonal}
\hlchaptermodality{176}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can read and use the impersonal se, where no person is named.}

Complete ES-C52-se-habla: write the sign and say who is doing the speaking.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[se habla español]{se habla español — nobody in particular}

\label{lesson:ES-C52-se-habla}



\begin{quote}
\emph{Se llama} — \textquotedblleft{}he calls himself.\textquotedblright{} You have had that \emph{se} since your third chapter. Here it is doing something you have seen on signs and never been able to parse.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: a sentence with nobody in it}]
\begin{quote}
\emph{\textbf{Se habla} español.} — Spanish is spoken here. \emph{\textbf{Se come} bien.} — One eats well here. / The food is good.
\end{quote}

Look for the person doing it. There is not one, and there is not meant to be. \emph{Se habla español} does not tell you \textbf{who} speaks Spanish — it tells you that Spanish gets spoken, and that is the entire content.

English has to work harder to be that vague. It reaches for a passive (\textquotedblleft{}Spanish is spoken\textquotedblright{}), or a fake subject (\textquotedblleft{}\textbf{they} speak Spanish here\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}\textbf{you} eat well there\textquotedblright{}), and neither is quite honest, because there is no \emph{they} and no \emph{you}.

Spanish just... leaves the person out. \textbf{The \emph{se} is the mark that says nobody is being named.}

This is why it is the natural voice of signs, notices and rules: \emph{se habla español}, \emph{se prohíbe fumar}, \emph{no se aceptan tarjetas}. A sign is not addressed by anyone to anyone. It simply reports that something is the case.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Se habla español\textquotedblright{} as if reading it off a window
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Se come bien\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\emph{Se habla español} — who is speaking? (\textbf{Nobody named} — that is the point.) What does the \emph{se} mark? (That \textbf{no person is being named}.) Next: why this form grew out of the one you already knew.
\end{tcolorbox}
